draft.title: checkify gives a custom VJP the wrong residual after a check
draft.body:
## Reproducer

On JAX 0.12.0.1 with the CPU runtime, run

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax.experimental import checkify

@jax.custom_vjp
def f(x):
    return jnp.sin(x)

f.defvjp(lambda x: (jnp.sin(x), x), lambda x, g: (g * jnp.cos(x),))

def checked_input(x):
    checkify.check(x < 100., "too large")
    return f(x)

g = jax.grad(lambda x: checkify.checkify(checked_input)(x)[1])
print(g(3.))
```

## Observed

The unpatched release returns 1.0. A residual forwarded from the function input resolves to an error leaf. Related staged calls raise output-arity errors.

## Expected

The derivative is cos(3), approximately −0.9899925.

## Proposed fix

Shift forwarded residual indices by the number of error leaves, forward the error from the custom forward rule, and handle the extra error and constant cotangents in the backward rule.

draft.title: A checkify Error has no public Boolean predicate inside jit
draft.body:
## Reproducer

On JAX 0.12.0.1 with the CPU runtime, run

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax.experimental import checkify

def positive_log(x):
    checkify.check(x > 0, "must be positive")
    return jnp.log(x)

@jax.jit
def safe_log(x):
    err, y = checkify.checkify(positive_log)(x)
    return jnp.where(err.has_error(), -jnp.inf, y)

print(safe_log(-1.))
```

## Observed

The release has no Error.has_error() method. The concrete-error accessors cannot supply a predicate while tracing.

## Expected

A public predicate should select −inf for this input, stay false for a successful check and preserve mapped dimensions.

## Proposed fix

Combine the error predicates with logical OR, with a false result for an empty error set. Expose this as a traceable method and test it under jit and vmap.

draft.title: A custom JVP closing over an array loses a preceding checkify error
draft.body:
## Reproducer

On JAX 0.12.0.1 with the CPU runtime, run

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax.experimental import checkify

c = jnp.arange(3.) + 1.
@jax.custom_jvp
def f(x):
    return x * c
f.defjvp(lambda p, t: (f(p[0]), t[0] * c))

def g(x):
    checkify.check(x[0] < 100., "too large")
    return f(x).sum()

(err, _), _ = jax.jvp(checkify.checkify(g), (jnp.full(3, 200.),), (jnp.ones(3),))
print(err.get())
```

## Observed

The error is silently lost and get() returns None.

## Expected

The check failed before the custom call, so the returned error should contain “too large”.

## Proposed fix

Read the leading error leaves from the staged inputs and tangents before skipping the closed-over constants for the JVP computation.

problems.title: Differentiating a staged checkified custom rule can fail on output arity
problems.summary: When the custom function introduces its first checked operation, its output carries more error effects than its input. Forwarding the smaller input error from the derivative rule produces too few outputs.

draft.title: Differentiating a staged checkified custom rule can fail on output arity
draft.body:
## Reproducer

On JAX 0.12.0.1 with the CPU runtime, run

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax.experimental import checkify

f = jax.custom_jvp(jnp.sin)
f.defjvp(lambda p, t: (jnp.sin(p[0]), jnp.cos(p[0]) * t[0]))
checked = jax.jit(checkify.checkify(f, errors=checkify.float_checks))
print(jax.grad(lambda x: checked(x)[1])(3.))
```

## Observed

The staged equation expects the error effects produced by sin. Its derivative forwards fewer leaves and raises ValueError while matching outputs.

## Expected

The gradient should be cos(3), and a check raised before a custom call should still reach its caller.

## Proposed fix

Pad the forwarded error with placeholders for any new output effects from the staged primal. Consume the matching number of error cotangents in the VJP.
